title: BST Search

description.intro:
A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree if, for every node:

All the values on its left subtree are less than or equal to the node's value.
All the values on its right subtree are greater than or equal to the node's value.
Given the root of a binary search tree and a value, target, return true if the tree contains the target value, and false otherwise.
examples:
Example 2:
Same tree, target = 3
Output: false
The value 3 does not exist in the tree.
constraints: The number of nodes is at most 10^5
The value at each node is between 0 and 10^9
description.approach:
We implement the BST analogous of binary search over a sorted array.

complexity:
Time & Space Analysis
n: the number of nodes in the tree

h: the height of the tree

Time: O(h) - we only go down one path in the tree

Extra space: O(1)

tests.python:
def run_tests():
  # Test 1
  root1 = Node(5,
               Node(2,
                    None,
                    Node(4)),
               Node(9,
                    Node(9,
                         None,
                         Node(9)),
                    Node(11)))

  # Test 2: Empty tree
  root2 = None

  # Test 3: Single node
  root3 = Node(1)

  # Test 4: Perfect BST
  root4 = Node(4,
               Node(2,
                    Node(1),
                    Node(3)),
               Node(6,
                    Node(5),
                    Node(7)))

  # Test 5: Unbalanced BST
  root5 = Node(5,
               Node(3,
                    Node(2,
                         Node(1),
                         None),
                    Node(4)),
               None)

  tests = [
      (root1, 6, False),
      (root1, 9, True),
      (root1, 3, False),
      (root1, 4, True),
      (root2, 1, False),  # Empty tree
  ]

  for i, (root, target, want) in enumerate(tests):
    got = contains_target(root, target)
    assert got == want, f"\nfind(root{        i + 1}, {target}): got: {got}, want: {want}\n"

run_tests()
